calculation_handling.description: Scope: Article 10.5.60 applies to ancillary buildings or structures in the Residential Zone category that are ancillary to dwelling units or residential buildings.
An ancillary building in the Residential Zone category may not be used for living accommodation.
calculation_handling.gaps: Living accommodation is not a vocab.uses token, so the prohibited use is described here rather than keyed. Whether an ancillary building is used for living accommodation is a design/use fact we do not evaluate.

units.disclosure: An accessory building (such as a garage or shed) in a residential zone cannot be used as living space. We do not check how an accessory building will be used.

calculation_handling.description: An ancillary building in the Residential Zone category may have both food preparation facilities and sanitary facilities if it is for indoor amenity space required by the By-law.
calculation_handling.gaps: Facilities and amenity-space purpose are design facts with no vocab token; not evaluated.

units.disclosure: An accessory building used as required indoor amenity space may have both a kitchen and washroom facilities. We do not check accessory building fit-out.

calculation_handling.description: An ancillary building in the Residential Zone category used for any purpose other than required indoor amenity space may have either food preparation facilities or sanitary facilities, but not both.
calculation_handling.gaps: Keyed PERMIT (the clause grants either facility); its 'but not both' limb is a restriction on the same permission and is described here, not keyed as a separate PROHIBIT. Design facts with no vocab token; not evaluated.

units.disclosure: Any other accessory building may have a kitchen or washroom facilities, but not both. We do not check accessory building fit-out.

calculation_handling.description: In the Residential Zone category, no above-ground part of an ancillary building or structure may be erected before the main walls and roof of a residential building on the same lot are erected and completed.
calculation_handling.gaps: A construction-sequencing rule; it constrains timing, not the built envelope, and is not evaluated.

units.disclosure: An accessory building cannot be built above ground before the house on the same lot has its main walls up and roof completed. This is a construction-timing rule we do not evaluate.

10.5.60.1(1).explanation: The rules in Article 10.5.60 cover accessory buildings and structures (garages, sheds and similar) in all residential zones when they serve homes or residential buildings.

10.5.60.1(2).explanation: An accessory building in a residential zone cannot be used as living space.

10.5.60.1(3).explanation: An accessory building used as required indoor amenity space may have both kitchen and washroom facilities; any other accessory building may have one or the other, but not both.

10.5.60.1(4).explanation: In residential zones, an accessory building cannot be built above ground until the house on the lot has its main walls built and roof completed.
